question: A Canadian grocery receipt shows 0% GST/HST on ordinary milk, bread and vegetables. Does that mean this store has stopped charging GST/HST on all products?
generated_answer:
No, it doesn't mean the store has stopped charging GST/HST on all products. In Canada, certain basic groceries, such as milk, bread, and vegetables, are exempt from the Goods and Services Tax (GST) and Harmonized Sales Tax (HST). This exemption is mandated by the federal and provincial governments to help make essential food items more affordable for consumers.

The 0% GST/HST rate you see on these items is a result of this exemption, not a decision by the store to stop charging tax. Other products that are not exempt, such as prepared foods, snacks, and non-essential items, will still be subject to the applicable GST/HST rate, which varies by province.

So, if you look at the receipt, you'll likely see that other items have the standard GST/HST rate applied, while the exempt groceries show 0% tax.
